Contamination-aware Bayesian integration of probability and non-probability samples

Source: R/mixture_fit.R
mixture_fit.Rd

Fits a regression model to a trusted probability (P) sample and a non-probability (NP) sample in which an unknown subset of observations may be incompatible with the target model ("contaminated"). Each NP observation carries a latent indicator of compatibility; compatible observations are pooled with the P sample to estimate the target regression, while contaminated observations are absorbed by a separate component.

Usage

mixture_fit(
  formula,
  prob_data,
  nonprob_data,
  family = c("gaussian", "binomial", "poisson"),
  model = c("Mjoint", "M0", "M1"),
  leverage = NULL,
  n_iter = 3000,
  burnin = 1500,
  thin = 1,
  seed = NULL,
  prior = mixture_prior(),
  control = mixture_control(),
  na_action = c("omit", "fail"),
  verbose = FALSE
)

Arguments

formula

A two-sided model formula, e.g. y ~ x1 + x2. Offsets are not supported.

prob_data

Data frame with the probability (trusted) sample.

nonprob_data

Data frame with the non-probability sample. Must contain all variables used in formula.

family

One of "gaussian", "binomial" (logistic regression for a 0/1, logical or two-level factor response) or "poisson". A family object such as binomial() is also accepted (only its name is used; the links are fixed to identity, logit and log respectively).

model

Contamination model: "Mjoint" (default), "M0" or "M1"; see the Model section.

leverage

Names of the design-matrix columns entering the covariate density of "Mjoint". NULL (default) selects all non-constant columns taking more than two distinct values in the P sample (i.e. continuous predictors; intercept and dummy variables are excluded).

n_iter

Total number of MCMC iterations, including burn-in.

burnin

Number of initial iterations discarded.

thin

Keep every thin-th post-burn-in draw.

seed

Optional random seed. When supplied the fit is reproducible and the global random-number stream is restored afterwards; when NULL the current stream is used.

prior

Prior hyperparameters, see mixture_prior().

control

Algorithm settings, see mixture_control().

na_action

"omit" (default) drops rows with missing values in any model variable, separately within each sample, and records how many were dropped; "fail" stops with an error if any are present.

verbose

If TRUE, report progress every 10% of iterations.

Value

An object of class bsm_fit, a list including

draws

matrix of retained posterior draws of the target-model coefficients (plus sigma2 for Gaussian), contamination and contamination_realized;

bad_draws

draws of the contaminating-component parameters;

filter_score

posterior compatibility probabilities \(s_j\) of the NP observations used in the fit;

indicator_entropy

binary entropy (nats) of each \(s_j\);

nonprob_rows

row names of nonprob_data used in the fit (after removing missing values), aligned with filter_score;

and settings needed by the methods summary.bsm_fit(), predict.bsm_fit(), plot.bsm_fit(), coef.bsm_fit() and as.matrix.bsm_fit().

Model

For P-sample units \(i\) the outcome follows the target model \(f(y_i \mid x_i, \theta)\) (Gaussian, logistic or Poisson regression with coefficients \(\beta\)). For NP units \(j\), $$z_j \sim \mathrm{Bernoulli}(\pi),$$ $$p(y_j, x_j \mid z_j = 1) = f(y_j \mid x_j, \theta)\, g_1(x_j),\qquad p(y_j, x_j \mid z_j = 0) = h(y_j \mid x_j, \phi)\, g_0(x_j).$$ The contaminating outcome density \(h\) depends on model:

"M0"

a covariate-free density: \(N(\mu_0, \tau^2)\) (Gaussian), \(Bernoulli(q)\) (binomial), \(Poisson(\lambda_0)\) (Poisson); and \(g_1 = g_0 = 1\).

"Mjoint"

as "M0", plus a covariate ("leverage") term for the continuous predictors \(x_c\) selected by leverage: \(g_1 = N(x_c; \hat\mu_P, \hat\Sigma_P)\) and \(g_0 = N(x_c; \hat\mu_P, c\,\hat\Sigma_P)\), where \(\hat\mu_P, \hat\Sigma_P\) are the P-sample mean and covariance (fixed plug-in values) and \(c\) is control$c_infl. NP points far from the P covariate distribution (in Mahalanobis distance) are thereby more likely to be flagged.

"M1"

a rival regression of the same family with its own coefficients \(\beta_{bad}\) (and variance, Gaussian case); no covariate term.

Because the P sample contributes only to the target component, the labels of the two mixture components are identified (no label switching).

Algorithm

A data-augmentation Gibbs sampler alternates between (1) drawing every \(z_j\) from its Bernoulli full conditional, (2) drawing \(\pi \sim Beta(a_\pi + \sum z_j, b_\pi + n_{NP} - \sum z_j)\), (3) updating the target-model parameters given the P sample plus the NP units with \(z_j = 1\), and (4) updating the contaminating component given the units with \(z_j = 0\). Step (3) is family specific and follows the original implementation:

  • Gaussian: conjugate normal / inverse-gamma Gibbs updates.

  • Binomial: Polya-Gamma augmentation (Polson, Scott and Windle, 2013), with PG(1, z) variables drawn from a pg_terms-term truncation of their sum-of-gammas representation plus a tail-mean correction. This is a close approximation rather than an exact PG draw.

  • Poisson: a Metropolis-Hastings step with a Laplace (Gaussian) proposal centred at the conditional mode, which is found by irls_steps Newton iterations from the current value. Once these iterations have converged the proposal is state independent and the step is an exact independence sampler; otherwise it is an approximation. The post-burn-in acceptance rate is reported by summary.bsm_fit().

The filter score of NP unit \(j\) is the Rao-Blackwellised posterior probability of compatibility, \(s_j = E[P(z_j = 1 \mid \cdot) \mid data]\), averaged over all post-burn-in iterations (thinning affects only the stored parameter draws).

Contamination summaries

Two posterior quantities are reported: contamination is \(1 - \pi\), the population-level probability that an NP unit is contaminated (as in the original code); contamination_realized is the fraction of the observed NP units allocated to the contaminating component at each iteration, \(1 - \sum_j z_j / n_{NP}\).

\(1 - \pi\) is the weight of the contaminating component, which is identified only to the extent that the two components can be told apart. With the covariate-free contaminating densities of "M0"/"Mjoint", compatible units that fit both components about equally well are partly allocated to the contaminating one, and the "Mjoint" covariate term also allocates compatible units in the tails of the P covariate distribution to it. In simulations with binomial and Poisson outcomes this led to posterior means of \(1 - \pi\) well above the true share of contaminated units, while the target coefficients remained accurate (see the package vignettes). Read \(1 - \pi\) as a conservative measure of incompatibility rather than a count of contaminated units.

References

Polson, N. G., Scott, J. G. and Windle, J. (2013). Bayesian inference for logistic models using Polya-Gamma latent variables. Journal of the American Statistical Association, 108(504), 1339-1349.

Diebolt, J. and Robert, C. P. (1994). Estimation of finite mixture distributions through Bayesian sampling. Journal of the Royal Statistical Society: Series B, 56(2), 363-375.

See also

baseline_fit() for probability-only and naively pooled reference fits, overlap_diagnostics() for covariate-overlap checks, simulate_mixture_data() for example data.

Examples

d <- simulate_mixture_data("gaussian", n_prob = 100, n_nonprob = 100,
                           contamination = 0.3, seed = 1)
fit <- mixture_fit(y ~ x1, d$prob, d$nonprob, family = "gaussian",
                   n_iter = 600, burnin = 200, seed = 42)
fit
#> Bayesian contamination-mixture fit (bayesSampleMix)
#> Family: gaussian   Model: Mjoint
#> n_P = 100, n_NP = 100, 400 posterior draws
#> 
#> Posterior mean coefficients:
#> (Intercept)          x1 
#>        2.08        4.97 
#> 
#> Contamination (1 - pi): 0.323  [95% CrI 0.224, 0.419]
summary(fit)
#> Bayesian contamination-mixture fit (bayesSampleMix)
#> Call: mixture_fit(formula = y ~ x1, prob_data = d$prob, nonprob_data = d$nonprob, 
#>     family = "gaussian", n_iter = 600, burnin = 200, seed = 42)
#> Family:  Gaussian (identity link)
#> Model:   Mjoint (contaminating density + covariate leverage term)
#> Leverage covariates: x1  (inflation c = 4)
#> Samples: n_P = 100, n_NP = 100
#> MCMC:    600 iterations, burn-in 200, thin 1 -> 400 draws
#> 
#> Target-model coefficients (posterior; 95% credible intervals):
#>             mean     sd 2.5%  50% 97.5% ess    mcse
#> (Intercept) 2.08 0.0792 1.92 2.08  2.22 357 0.00419
#> x1          4.97 0.0821 4.83 4.97  5.14 393 0.00414
#> 
#> Error variance:
#>         mean    sd  2.5%   50% 97.5% ess    mcse
#> sigma2 0.956 0.105 0.774 0.948  1.18 297 0.00608
#> 
#> Contamination:
#>                         mean     sd  2.5%   50% 97.5% ess    mcse
#> contamination          0.323 0.0515 0.224 0.321 0.419 230 0.00339
#> contamination_realized 0.316 0.0288 0.260 0.320 0.370 231 0.00189
#> 
#> Filter scores of NP units (s_j = posterior P(compatible)):
#>   expected compatible units: 68.6 of 100; units with s_j < 0.5: 26; mean entropy: 0.212
head(filter_scores(fit))
#>            1            2            3            4            5            6 
#> 3.329450e-04 5.697014e-35 9.349462e-01 9.238125e-01 4.716416e-17 4.039575e-06
